context: Make a bare model-id collision between two Anthropic-surface backends fail closed, before the overlapping 29-model OpenCode catalog is introduced.
root_causes: _build_model_index assigns index[key] = backend with no conflict detection, so a duplicate bare id is resolved by insertion order and the loser is discarded silently.
kimi-k3 currently resolves to the kimi backend because the kimi seed loop runs last, which is an ordering accident rather than a recorded decision.
_BACKENDS_WITH_ROWS is derived from frozenset(_MODEL_INDEX.values()), so a silent overwrite also changes which backends count as rows-owning for qualified routing.
evidence: surface_registry._build_model_index writes index[_normalize_model(model_name)] = backend for config rows, then seeds _CODEX_MODELS and _KIMI_MODELS over the same dict with no duplicate check.
The OpenCode Go catalog probed live on 2026-08-11 contains deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-flash and kimi-k3, all already claimed bare by other backends.
solutions: Detect a bare id claimed by two different backends during index construction and fail closed with a message naming the id and both backends.
Keep an identical re-declaration of the same id to the same backend harmless, so ordinary config duplication does not become an outage.
Apply the same rule inside the builder so cross_check_anthropic_models' independently rebuilt fresh_index cannot diverge from resolution.
acceptance_criteria: A synthetic duplicate bare id across two backends fails the index build with a message naming the id and both backends.
The real backend set builds clean, proving the guard is not vacuous.
A duplicate id mapping to the same backend is accepted.
No currently resolvable model id changes backend.
legacy_risk_reason: module coverage is 91%, so the low-coverage trigger does not apply; legacy-safe is selected on blast radius. _build_model_index feeds _MODEL_INDEX, which _BACKENDS_WITH_ROWS is derived from, which decides rows-owning vs rowless qualified routing for claude, codex, deepseek, kimi, copilot and auggie. A regression here silently changes which backend serves a model.
